packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

UNVERIFIED IMAGE-ONLY READING — PACKET 02

Isolation: I inspected only this packet's PROMPT.md and supplied images, and local crops derived from those images. I did not read source metadata, consult a catalogue or edition, use the web, inspect repository or memory files, consult an earlier reading, or attempt work/author identification. I had not been shown a proposed identification for this packet.

Image-only layout survey: Both images are upright. Each has two columns of small, brown, heavily abbreviated cursive writing. In image-001 the columns run almost to the lower cut edge. Image-002 has a short upper right-column block, a conspicuous blank horizontal gap, then a longer block starting with a larger initial-like stroke. There is no legible running title and no visible colored rubric or colored initial. Some paragraph-like or enlarged letter forms occur within the continuous text. I cannot confidently distinguish underlining from long abbreviation strokes. There is no regular interlinear or marginal commentary apparatus. Image-001 has a small isolated word-like marginal addition at the right, not transcribed here. Holes and tears interrupt the top and other parts of both leaves; the bottommost lines are cut off. The darker black shapes near the middle/lower portions are holes or marks and should not automatically be interpreted as letterforms. Whether the text itself is commentary cannot be established from this layout.

Procedure and coverage: I inspected complete-image overviews for layout, then eight native-pixel crops from the original JPEGs. Originals are image-001.jpg 5203 × 7070 and image-002.jpg 5176 × 7019. The layout overviews were reduced to 1700 pixels high. The transcription crops were not resized or rotated, and no contrast or sharpening transform was applied. Coordinates (left, top, right, bottom), origin upper left:
image-001: i1-left-top (430,810,2220,2230); i1-right-top (2440,810,4320,2230); i1-left-mid (430,2730,2220,4180); i1-right-mid (2440,2200,4320,3650).

Top/middle crops overlap slightly in some columns. Overlapping lines are not additional text.

Reading limitation: Native-scale inspection clarifies the individual strokes but does not let me securely resolve this compressed cursive hand into continuous sentences. I checked other regions instead of relying on the first faint region. The following is a deliberately fragmentary reading, not a reconstructed text. I cannot honestly supply a checkable continuous passage from these images on this pass. Several repeated letter groups look like “materialis”, “formalis”, and possibly “efficiens”, but the latter in particular is uncertain. These are readings of visible glyph groups, not conclusions about the subject or source.

Textual presentation limits: I cannot distinguish a quoted lemma from connecting commentary securely here, and therefore have not assigned quotation marks or source labels. I see no deletion or interlinear insertion that I can identify confidently; some heavy horizontal strokes may be abbreviations, overwriting, or cancellation, but I do not classify them as a deletion without greater certainty. Most lower-column text remains unread. The photographs already give a wide view; another wider crop would not itself solve the handwriting difficulty.
